A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same 24-page paper, including Appendices A–F. Text and rendered-page comparisons establish identical scientific content; differences are confined to the version/date stamp and bibliography.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendices C–F report original experiments on algorithmic tasks, MiniPile perplexity, MMLU capability suppression, and recovery of information using activation probes.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results, including accuracy tables, allocation-policy comparisons, suppression analyses, and probe evaluations.

M1.justification: The NLPN rank-prefix parameterization, monitor–allocator–enforcer framework, training objective, Algorithm 1, and subject-suppression optimization procedure are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use Balanced Brackets, Length Comparison, Contains Substring, MiniPile, and the same MMLU subjects. No training or evaluation coverage changes.

E2.justification: The same five allocation policies are compared in Appendix C. The SVD comparison in Appendix D and standard-prompt, unhelpful-prompt, and probe comparisons in Appendix F are also retained.

E3.justification: Model configurations, rank sweeps, difficulty levels, validation-based calibration, accuracy targets of 80%, 90%, and 95%, and evaluation metrics and procedures are identical.

E4.justification: The difficulty-dependent degradation analysis, block/module sensitivity studies, selective subject suppression, and latent-information recovery analysis remain unchanged in Section 5 and Appendices C–F.

E5.justification: Uncertainty reporting is unchanged, including Figure 15's three-seed reporting and Appendix E's Benjamini–Hochberg correction at q = 0.05. No statistical procedures or run counts are added or revised.

E6.justification: All numerical results and plotted findings are identical. For example, Table 2 reports Pythia-1B Balanced Brackets accuracy of 99.3 ± 0.4% at rank index 0 in both versions.

T1.justification: Definition 3.1, the least-privilege optimization objective, rank-nesting reasoning, and Appendix B's mathematical arguments are unchanged. No definitions, derivations, or proofs are added or corrected.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution statement, and discussion retain the same claims about least-privilege deployment, reversible internal control, and selective capability suppression.

C2.justification: Interpretations and limitations are identical, including Appendix B's qualifications that rank is a capability proxy, capabilities need not be localized, and a privilege interface is not itself a safety solution.

D1.justification: Implementation and reproducibility information is unchanged, including SVD initialization, MiniPile training, beam-search hyperparameters, probe procedures, and the implementation repository disclosure.

R1.justification: No cited works or research-positioning arguments change. The existing Mouton et al. (2024) entry receives bibliographic metadata edits; references shifted between pages are retained.

P1.justification: v2 updates the arXiv version/date stamp and replaces the Mouton reference's incomplete URL and '24 p.' text with a full URL and 'Page 13.' Scientific prose and section structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: The longer reference entry reflows the bibliography, moving Yu and Huang (2019) from page 11 to page 12. Figures 1–15, Tables 1–4, and all appendix layouts remain identical.

improvement.justification: v2 supplies a more complete source locator for Mouton et al. (2024), a small editorial benefit. The methods, evidence, reasoning, limitations, and substantive presentation remain unchanged, so this isolated bibliographic repair does not materially alter overall paper quality.
